paper_metadata.title: TwinMarket: A Scalable Behavioral and Social Simulation for Financial Markets
paper_metadata.authors: Yuzhe Yang, Yifei Zhang, Minghao Wu, Kaidi Zhang, Yunmiao Zhang, Honghai Yu, Yan Hu, Benyou Wang

key_findings.finding: TwinMarket integrates LLM agents with a BDI cognitive architecture, a dynamic social network, and a realistic market environment to simulate financial markets, outperforming traditional ABMs in replicating stylized facts.
Ablation studies confirm that both the BDI framework and agent heterogeneity are essential for generating realistic fat tails, leverage effects, and volatility clustering.
Scaling the number of agents improves predictive accuracy (lower RMSE/MAE) and enriches emergent macro-level phenomena, supporting the scaling law.
The framework successfully reproduces emergent social and market phenomena such as opinion leaders, self-fulfilling prophecies, and rumor-induced market turbulence.
Micro-level agent behaviors (e.g., higher trading frequency correlating with lower returns) align with real-world investor data, validating behavioral fidelity.

new_concepts.name: BDI-driven LLM Agent
new_concepts.definition: An agent architecture where Beliefs, Desires, and Intentions guide perception, information-seeking, and trading decisions, enabling heterogeneous and adaptive behaviors grounded in cognitive science.
new_concepts.marketfish_relevance: Can be integrated into MarketFish to enhance agent realism, allowing for dynamic belief updates and goal-oriented decision-making that capture behavioral biases.

new_concepts.name: Dynamic Social Network Based on Trading Similarity
new_concepts.definition: A time-weighted graph where edges represent behavioral similarity between agents, enabling personalized information propagation and influence, with edge strengths decaying over time.
new_concepts.marketfish_relevance: Enables MarketFish to simulate information diffusion and social influence among agents, allowing study of herding, polarization, and opinion leader emergence.

new_concepts.name: Information Aggregation with Hot Score
new_concepts.definition: A mechanism that ranks and recommends social media posts to agents based on a score balancing popularity (upvotes) and recency, controlling each agent's perception field.
new_concepts.marketfish_relevance: Provides a realistic model of how agents selectively receive information, which can be used in MarketFish to simulate echo chambers and filter bubbles.

new_concepts.name: TwinMarket Framework
new_concepts.definition: A scalable multi-agent simulation platform combining LLM agents, BDI cognition, a dynamic social network, and an order-driven trading system to study micro-macro emergence in financial markets.
new_concepts.marketfish_relevance: Can serve as a blueprint for building a next-generation agent-based market simulator within MarketFish, replacing simpler rule-based models.

new_parameters.name: bdi_enabled
new_parameters.reason: Enables the Belief-Desire-Intention cognitive framework for agents, improving behavioral realism.

new_parameters.name: social_network_enabled
new_parameters.reason: Activates the dynamic social network and information propagation mechanisms.

new_parameters.name: similarity_threshold
new_parameters.reason: Minimum trading similarity to form an edge in the social graph; controls network density.

new_parameters.name: time_decay_factor
new_parameters.reason: Exponential decay rate for weighing past trades in computing similarity; higher values emphasize recent behavior.

new_parameters.name: hot_score_alpha
new_parameters.reason: Normalization constant for post recency in the hot score formula; set so that influence halves after ~2 weeks.

new_parameters.name: top_k_posts
new_parameters.reason: Number of top posts recommended to each agent daily from its neighbors.

new_parameters.name: llm_temperature
new_parameters.reason: Temperature for LLM calls; higher values increase output diversity but core decisions remain stable.

new_parameters.name: agent_activation_rate
new_parameters.reason: Fraction of agents active in trading each day; affects volume and market dynamics.

modify_existing.reason: Longer simulations needed to observe emergent phenomena; paper uses 5 months.
Replace simple heuristics with LLM-based reasoning to capture behavioral biases and adaptive strategies.

pipeline_implications.rationale: Introduce a stage where agents post, read, and repost on a simulated social media platform using the hot-score ranking, enabling information propagation. Modify the agent decision stage to incorporate BDI reasoning: belief update from news/social posts, desire-driven querying, intention-driven trading and posting actions. These changes are essential to replicate emergent market phenomena like herding and bubbles.
